 JUDGMENT The petitioner has filed this petition U/s 166 of Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of Rs.9,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

Brief averments of the petition are as under:
As per the case of the petitioner that, she is being minor and represented by her natural guardian father.
That, on 22.01.2019 at about 3.30 p.m., when the petitioner was riding the Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA05HY7442 on Ganakal main road, carefully and cautiously, observing all the traffic rules and regulations, when she reached near Pavani Famiy restaurant, Ganakal main road, Kengeri, Bengaluru at that time the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA41MB9194 came in rash and negligent manner,
endangering to human life, neglecting all the traffic rules and regulations, without blowing horn or giving any signal, came mindlessly and recklessly lost control of his car and dashed against minor petitioner's scooter.
As a result of which, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

It is further submitted that,
immediately after the accident petitioner was shifted to BGS Global Hospital as an inpatient.

Accordingly, petitioner has has spent huge amount towards medicine,
conveyance, nourishment food, attendant charges and other incidental charges etc.,

It is further submitted that, at the time of the accident petitioner was student, due to the injuries sustained in the SCCH14 4 MVC No.726/2019 said accident the petitioner was on rest even to this day due to the injuries sustained in the accident and in future also the petitioner is unable to participate in curricular activities in the school and college and she is brilliant student in the school.

It is further submitted that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent act of the Kumari Akshatha S vs The Branch Manager on 29 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101728172/
2 driver of the offending car.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that, the Kengeri Traffic police have registered the case in Crime No.0012/2019 against the driver of offending car for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC.
The respondents No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being owner of the vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, the petitioner prayed for awarding compensation with interest and cost.
3. In response to the notice, the respondent No.2 is absent and placed exparte and respondent No.1 is appeared before the Tribunal through its counsel and filed its written statement.

Further contended that, the respondents No.1 has denied the case of the petitioner as false and contended that the petition is not at all maintainable either in law or SCCH14 5 MVC No.726/2019 on facts.
Further contended that, this respondents has denied the age avocation and income of the deceased.
Further contended that, the compensation and interest as claimed by the petitioners are exorbitant and excessive.

Further denied all the allegations found in the petition other than those that are specifically admitted that, this respondent has issued a private car policy package policy bearing No.OG19 1701182500001866 in favour of 2 nd respondent in respect of New Maruthi Baleno Car having Engine & Chassis No.4453049 & MA3EWB22SJH552718 and is is valid from 03.11.2018 to 2.11.2019 and their liability, if any is strictly in terms and conditions.

Further contended that,
respondent No.2 willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving license to drive the same as on the date of the accident.

In fact the alleged accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding the motorcycle by the petitioner without possessing the driving license to ride the motorcycle and not having insurance to use that vehicle on the public road and not wearing safety headgear.
Thus the petitioner being guilt of violation of motorcycle rules and regulations, she is not entitled for any compensation by the SCCH14 6 MVC No.726/2019 hands of this court.

Further contended that, compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive,
exorbitant and it has no rationale.
The petitioner is not entitled to claim any compensation much less claimed Rs.9,00,000/ with interest at 9% p.a.,
Hence, on other grounds, the respondent No.1 has prayed for dismissal of the claim petition with costs.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that she sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 22.01.2019 at about 03.30 p.m., near Pavani Famiy restaurant, Ganakal main road, Kengeri, Bengaluru, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of car bearing No.KA41MB9194?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

sentences.text: My findings on the above issues are as under: Issue No.1 : Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.3 : As per final order, for the following:
 SCCH14 9 MVC No.726/2019  REASONS 9.
Issue No.1:

In this case, the petitioner has filed this petition seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident that occurred on 22.01.2019 due to actionable negligence on the part of driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA41MB9194, when the minor petitioner was riding Honda Activa Scooter on Ganakal main road, near Pavani Restaurant, Kengeri,
Bengaluru, at that time the driver of offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA41MB9194 came in a high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's scooter etc.
, Per contra respondent No.1 has denied the same, it is the main contention of the respondent No.1 is that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the scooter by the petitioner.

Without possessing the driving license to ride the scooter and not having insurance to use that vehicle on the public road and not wearing safety headgear, she being guilty of violation of motorcycle rules and regulations, as such she is not entitled for any compensation from this respondent.
In order to prove her case, the petitioner examined her father/natural guardian as PW.1, who has reiterated the petition averments in his examinationin chief affidavit.

Further the petitioner examined one Dr.Raju K.P, Senior Consultant, Orthopedic Surgeon, at BGS Hospital, Bengaluru as PW.2 and in all got marked Ex.P.1 to 14 documents.
11.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has examined its Senior Executive as Rw.1 nor marked any documents on its behalf.

12. With regard to the negligence part is concerned, in the cross examination of PW.1 made by learned advocate for respondent No.1, the PW1 deposed that, Honda Activa vehicle standing in his name and it is a 108 cc vehicle and he himself gave it to his daughter to ride the same.
Further stated that, at the time of the accident, his daughter was 14 years old and nobody accompanied with her at the time of the accident.
Further admits that, his daughter had no driving license to ride the same.
Further stated that, his daughter was riding the said scooter since six months from the date of the accident.
Further admits that, even though SCCH14 11 MVC No.726/2019 his daughter has no right to ride the said scooter, she rode the same in a main road, as such, the accident had occurred.
Further denied that, the accident had not occurred as stated by him in his petition and examination inchief.
Further denied that, he himself is responsible for the accident.
Further denied that, he colluding with police and filed false case to get compensation.
Further stated that, he insured his vehicle with Bajaj Insurance company and not obtained any compensation from it.

However he has not produced any such documents in this regard.

Admittedly, he is not an eye witness to this accident, but it is clear that, petitioner was minor at the time of the accident and she was riding the scooter alone in a main road and due to her fault also the accident had occurred.

13. Besides on perusal of Ex.P.1 FIR with complaint reveals that, police constable has given requisition with regard to the accident on the date of the accident itself stating that, on 22.01.2019 at about 3.45 p.m., he received information that accident had occurred at Ganakallu main SCCH14 12 MVC No.726/2019 road then he went to the said place and after inquiry he found that offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA41MB9194 came in a nice road in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against to the petitioner's scooter which was coming from Srinivasa Colony and then dashed two pedestrians who are coming by the side of the road and petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the said accident, as such, she got admitted to BGS hospital etc.,
Accordingly, Kengeri Traffic police have registered FIR against the driver of the offending car in their crime No.0012/2019 for the offences punishable U/s 279 and 337 of IPC.

Further on perusal of Ex.P.2 spot mahazar with sketch reveals that, the accident had occurred at junction and at the time of the accident the petitioner came from BSK 6th Stage, 11th block towards main road and at that time the offending car came from nice road towards Aditya Bakery and when the petitioner entered into circle about to take turn to the left side towards Aditya Bakery the offending car dashed against the petitioner's scooter.

Admittedly, the manner of the accident reveals that, at the time of the accident petitioner who is the minor came in a SCCH14 13 MVC No.726/2019 rash and negligent manner and she could not control her vehicle and at the same time the driver of the offending vehicle also in the junction without controlling the speed of his vehicle dashed to the petitioner's scooter.
Admittedly, complainant not an eye witness, he came to the spot only after hearing the information of the accident.

According to Ex.P.3 IMV report it is clear that, head light assembly, pannel, handle bar, front right side shape, rear right side shape of the petitioner's scooter has been damaged and front wind screen glass, right side portion of bumper, front right side, front right side head light assembled of offending car has been damaged and according to IMV inspector the accident was not taken place due to any mechanical defects of both vehicles and brake system of both vehicle were in order.
Admittedly, the damages are caused to both vehicles reveals that, both petitioner and the driver of the offending vehicle were in high speed at the time of the accident.
So, due to fault of the both of them the accident had occurred.
Even on perusal of Ex.P.4 - wound certificate reveals that, petitioner had sustained injuries in the said accident.

SCCH14 14 MVC No.726/2019 It is the specific contention of the petitioner's counsel is that, even though the petitioner was minor at the time of the accident and not holding driving license no contributing negligence filed on her in the accidednt when the charge sheet has been filed against the driver of the offending car.

In this regard he has relied upon the decision reported in 2018 ACJ Kumari Akshatha S vs The Branch Manager on 29 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101728172/

sentences.text: Therefore, I am of the considered opinion that, the SCCH14 15 MVC No.726/2019 minor contributory negligence is fixed on the part of the minor petitioner is at 15% and major contributory negligence on the part of driver of the offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA41MB9194 at 85%.
Hence, I answer the Issue No.1 partly in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:
This issue relates to the quantum of compensation to be awarded to the petitioner and liability to pay the same.
It is the case of the petitioner that, after the accident she was treated as an inpatient at BGS Hospital, Bengaluru from 22.01.2019 to 26012019 for a period of 5 days.
In this regard she has produced two discharge summaries at Ex.P.6 and inpatient case sheet at Ex.P.12.
The contents of these respective medical documents makes it very clear with regard to the gravity of the injuries sustained by the petitioner.

As per the evidence of the PW.1, petitioner is still under treatment and could not participate in curricular activities in her school and she has lost her curricular activities and also affecting her daily activities till date.

By taking into consideration of the duration of the treatment as Inpatient, Outpatient, continued follow up, I am of the considered opinion, the SCCH 14 16 MVC No.726/2019 petitioner has suffered severely due to the accidental injuries.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of a sum of Rs.30,000/ towards Pain and sufferings.
Further, it can be said that the PW.1 must have incurred some amount for transportation and also spent some amount towards attendant charges, food and nourishment.
Thus, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.5,000/ towards Attendant, food, conveyance and other incidental expenses.

15. It is stated in the petition as well as in the evidence of P.W.1 that, she has spent Rs.1,41,520/
towards hospital charges, medicines, conveyance, nourishment etc.
In order to substantiate the same, the petitioner has produced 5Medical Bills at Ex.P.8 amounting to Rs.1,41,520/ and 1 Prescription at Ex.P.9.
Admittedly petitioner has produced inpatient receipt only to the extent of Rs.59,608/ out of Rs.1,39,608/.

During the course of crossexamination PW.1 admitted that, he has paid medical bills amount by way of cash, he has not produced any receipts for payment of entire medical bills as hospital authority has not given receipts.

Any how, petitioner was an inpatient Kumari Akshatha S vs The Branch Manager on 29 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101728172/

sentences.text: Taking SCCH14 17 MVC No.726/2019 into consideration of the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner must have incurred expenses towards medicines and treatment.

Hence, I am of the considered opinion that,
the petitioner is entitled for a compensation of Rs.1,41,520/ towards Medical Expenses.
16.
TOWARDS DISABILITY & LOSS OF AMENITIES:
The PW.1 deposed that, due to the accidental injuries, his daughter is suffering from disability.

She cannot walk for long distance, claims stairs ups and down, sit and squat on the floor, stand for long period, play and participate in any sports activities,
frequently suffering from ill health problems, often get pain in her entire right leg, do any manual normal children's activities.
During the course of crossexamination he admits that, at the time of the accident his daughter was studying 8th standard, now she studying 9th standard.

Further stated that, due to the accidental injuries his daughter was not going to school for a period of two months and in this regard he can produce the documents, but later he has not produced any such documents.
SCCH14 18 MVC No.726/2019

In this regard petitioner also examined Dr.Raju K.P.
Senior Consultant, Orthopaedic Surgeon at BGS Hospital as PW.2, he has deposed before this tribunal that, petitioner has sustained fracture shaft of right femur, she underwent surgery on 23.01.2019 for closed reduction internal fixation with interlocking nailing to right femur.
Recently he examined the petitioner and she has complains like, pain and limp in the right hip and knee with bad secondary healed scar over right leg.
She has difficulty while sitting on the floor, squatting and while climbing the stairs, standing on both legs, standing on affected leg, kneeling down etc., and to participate in sports activity.
She has limited right knee movement.
Further he assessed lower limb disability at 56% and whole body disability at 18.6%.
During the course of crossexamination he admitted that, the problems as stated in para No.4 of his affidavit has been stated by the patient when she came to their hospital for followup treatment.
There is no bone loss at fracture site.
No infection and no other puse formation at fracture site.
The fracture is united and condition of the patient was satisfactory.
Further contended that, loss of SCCH14 19 MVC No.726/2019 muscle power is reduced to 1 grade.
There is no restrictions in the ankle but there is restriction at hip around 25 degree and knee joint at 202 degree approximately.
Further contended that, he has not followed the guidelines of 2018 while assessing disability and he has followed 2001 guidelines.
He has advised for removal of implants.
After removal of implants the percentage of disability may be reduced in some extent.
Further denied that, whether the disability which assessed by him, is not permanent one as the petitioner is tender in age.
Admittedly, PW.2 has not followed recent guidelines for assessing the disability, but after following old guidelines he has assessed disability.
Further after removal of implants percentage of disability will be come down according to him.

Even the problems as stated by him above is as per say of Kumari Akshatha S vs The Branch Manager on 29 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101728172/
8 petitioner.

sentences.text: Further fracture is united and condition of the petitioner is also satisfactory.
Even he has not properly stated that, the disability which assessed by him is permanent one or not.
Such being the fact that, I am of the view that, the percentage of the whole body assessed by him is on higher side.

Further according SCCH14 20 MVC No.726/2019 to Ex.P.6 at the time of discharge condition of the petitioner is normal, therefore, I am of the view that, petitioner has not sustained 18.6% of whole body disability.

So by considering over the evidence of PW.1 and 2 and according to Ex.P.4, 6,
7, 12 to 14 petitioner has sustained permanent disability of 10% to the whole body.
There is no evidence to believe that performance of the petitioner in studies was poor when compared to her performance during previous year.
However, she is suffering from permanent disability of 10%.

Hon'ble Supreme Court has held ruling reported in ILR 2013 KAR 4891 (Master Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager) as under:
(a) Though it is difficult to have an accurate assessment of compensation in the case of children suffering disability on account of a motor vehicle accident, having regard to the relevant factors, precedents and the approach of various High Courts, that the appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment attendant, etc., should be, if the disability is above 10% and up 30% to the SCCH14 21 MVC No.726/2019 whole body, Rs.3 lakhs; upto 60% Rs.4 lakhs; upto 90%, Rs.5 lakhs and above 90%, it should be 6 lakhs,.

sentences.text: For permanent disability upto 10%, it should be Rs. 1 lakh, unless there are exceptional circumstances to take different yardstick.
In the instant case, the disability is to the tune of 18%.
Appellant had a longer period of hospitalization for about two months causing also inconvenience and loss of earning to the parents".
The said ruling is applicable to this case.
Further as per the evidence doctor the petitioner has to live with said disability throughout her life.
She has got several difficulties which may persist in future.
PW.2 confirms that the petitioner is having several difficulties, such difficulties result in loss of amenities.
The petitioner is entitled for a compensation of Rs.1,00,000/ towards disability and loss of amenities.
There is no evidence regarding requirement of future treatment to the petitioner.

17. LOSS OF INCOME TO PW.1 DURING THE PERIOD OF TAKING TREATMENT BY MINOR PETITIONER;
SCCH14 22 MVC No.726/2019 Further it is pertinent here to note that the petitioner has sustained fracture shaft of right femur and she took inpatient for a period of 5 days, the PW1 might have prevented from doing his duty/work for a period of two months.
In this case, the PW1 has not stated about his avocation and income at the time of alleged accident.

Hence, in the absence of any documents in this regard, this Tribunal has assessed the income of the PW1 at Rs.10,000/ p.m.
notionally as he admitted in his cross examination that he is practicing advocate.
Hence, the PW.1 is entitled for Rs.20,000/ under the head of loss of income during laid up period.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,16,520/.
In view of findings given by me on issue No.1 petitioner is entitled 85% of above compensation amount and which comes at Rs.2,69,042/ which can be rounded off Rs.2,69,000/.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled Rs.2,69,000/ only.

Liability:
19.
The respondents are the insurer and owner of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA41 MB9194.
It is proved that, the accident in question has taken place due to negligence of petitioner and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending car.

This tribunal also came to conclusion that, petitioner has contributed 15% of the negligence and driver SCCH14 24 MVC No.726/2019 of the offending car has contributed 85% of the negligence in the accident.
The respondent No.1 has admitted about the issuance of the insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 and policy was in force as on the date of the accident.

So, when the policy was in force, the respondent No.1 being insurer and respondent No.2 being owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.1 to indemnify the respondent No.2 and to compensate to the petitioner.

By considering the present days FD rate of interest in the nationalized bank it is just and necessary to direct the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation amount with interest at the rate of 7% p.a.,
from the date of petition till the date of payment.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
20. ISSUE No.3:

sentences.text: The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
SCCH14 25 MVC No.726/2019

The petitioner is entitled for a compensation of Rs.2,69,000/ with interest @ 7% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondents 1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner with interest.
The respondent No.1 being insurer is liable to deposit the amount before Tribunal within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit, Rs.1,50,000/ shall be released in favour of minor petitioner father as natural guardian and remaining balance amount shall be kept in fixed deposit in the name of minor petitioner in any nationalized or schedule bank, till she attains the age of majority and natural guardian of minor petitioner i.e., father is at liberty to withdraw interest accrued thereon periodically for welfare of the minor petitioner.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.issue:
4. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that she sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 22.01.2019 at about 03.30 p.m., near Pavani Famiy restaurant, Ganakal main road, Kengeri, Bengaluru, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of car bearing No.KA41MB9194?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Accordingly, Kengeri Traffic police have registered FIR against the driver of the offending car in their crime No.0012/2019 for the offences punishable U/s 279 and 337 of IPC.
Admittedly, the manner of the accident reveals that, at the time of the accident petitioner who is the minor came in a SCCH14 13 MVC No.726/2019 rash and negligent manner and she could not control her vehicle and at the same time the driver of the offending vehicle also in the junction without controlling the speed of his vehicle dashed to the petitioner's scooter.
Admittedly, complainant not an eye witness, he came to the spot only after hearing the information of the accident.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of a sum of Rs.30,000/ towards Pain and sufferings.
Further as per the evidence doctor the petitioner has to live with said disability throughout her life.
The petitioner is entitled for a compensation of Rs.1,00,000/ towards disability and loss of amenities.
There is no evidence regarding requirement of future treatment to the petitioner.
In this case, the PW1 has not stated about his avocation and income at the time of alleged accident.
Hence, in the absence of any documents in this regard, this Tribunal has assessed the income of the PW1 at Rs.10,000/ p.m.
notionally as he admitted in his cross examination that he is practicing advocate.
Hence, the PW.1 is entitled for Rs.20,000/ under the head of loss of income during laid up period.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Thus, I am of the considered opinion that, the SCCH14 23 MVC No.726/2019 petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following heads;
1. Pain and sufferings Rs. 30,000/
2. Nourishment, conveyance and Rs. 5,000/ attendant charges 3.
Medical expenses Rs. 1,41,520/
4. Loss of amenities Rs. 1,00,000/
5. Loss of income to PW.1 during Rs. 20,000/ the period of taking treatment by minor petitioner 6.
Future Medical Expenses Rs. 20,000/ Total Rs. 3,16,520/
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,16,520/.
In view of findings given by me on issue No.1 petitioner is entitled 85% of above compensation amount and which comes at Rs.2,69,042/ which can be rounded off Rs.2,69,000/.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled Rs.2,69,000/ only.
Liability:
19.
It is proved that, the accident in question has taken place due to negligence of petitioner and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending car.
This tribunal also came to conclusion that, petitioner has contributed 15% of the negligence and driver SCCH14 24 MVC No.726/2019 of the offending car has contributed 85% of the negligence in the accident.
So, when the policy was in force, the respondent No.1 being insurer and respondent No.2 being owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.1 to indemnify the respondent No.2 and to compensate to the petitioner.
By considering the present days FD rate of interest in the nationalized bank it is just and necessary to direct the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation amount with interest at the rate of 7% p.a.,
from the date of petition till the date of payment.
20. ISSUE No.3:
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled for a compensation of Rs.2,69,000/ with interest @ 7% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondents 1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner with interest.
The respondent No.1 being insurer is liable to deposit the amount before Tribunal within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit, Rs.1,50,000/ shall be released in favour of minor petitioner father as natural guardian and remaining balance amount shall be kept in fixed deposit in the name of minor petitioner in any nationalized or schedule bank, till she attains the age of majority and natural guardian of minor petitioner i.e., father is at liberty to withdraw interest accrued thereon periodically for welfare of the minor petitioner.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
